title: Optimal-rate regret bound for Hedge with convex prediction
statement:
Consider prediction with expert advice using $N \ge 2$ experts over $T \ge 1$ rounds, where predictions take values in a convex set $S \subseteq \bbr$. Let $\ell : \bbr \times \Omega \to \bbr$ be a loss function, let $p_t(i) \in S$ be the prediction of expert $i$ at round $t$, and let $o_t \in \Omega$ be the outcome at round $t$; assume that for every round $t$ the map $x \mapsto \ell(x, o_t)$ is convex on $S$, and that all induced losses $\ell(p_t(i), o_t)$ lie in $[0,1]$. Run the Hedge algorithm with learning rate $\eta_{\mathrm{tight}} = \sqrt{8\ln N / T}$, predicting at each round the Hedge weighted average $\widehat{x}_t = \sum_i p_t(i)\, w_{t}(i) \in S$, where the weights $w_t$ form the Hedge distribution built from the induced losses through the first $t$ rounds. Then the cumulative loss of these predictions exceeds the best expert's loss in hindsight by at most $\sqrt{\tfrac{T}{2}\ln N}$:
\[
  \sum_{t} \ell\bigl(\widehat{x}_t,\, o_t\bigr) \;-\; \min_{i}\, \sum_{t} \ell\bigl(p_t(i),\, o_t\bigr)
  \;\le\; \sqrt{\tfrac{T}{2}\ln N}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: S is a convex subset of the reals
every expert prediction lies in S
for each round the loss x ↦ ℓ(x, oₜ) is convex on S
the induced loss sequence is valid (all losses in [0,1])
the learning rate is η_tight = √(8 ln N / T)
replaced:
Under the same convexity hypotheses, with $T > 0$, $N > 1$, and the learning rate set
to $\eta^* = \texttt{optimalEtaTight}\,N\,T$, the regret satisfies
\[
  \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{pred}}_T
    - \min_{i}\,\sum_{t} \ell(p_t(i),\, o_t)
  \;\le\;
  \sqrt{\tfrac{T}{2}\ln N}.
\]
